newsitem.title: SPAIN: CanalSatelite open to share Spain soccer TV rights.
newsitem.headline: CanalSatelite open to share Spain soccer TV rights.

text.p: Audiovisual Sport said on Monday that CanalSatelite, which holds exclusive pay-TV rights to view Spain's premier soccer matches, was "disposed" to talking about sharing those rights with rival digital platform Via Digital.

Telefonica de Espana, which leads Via Digital, recently bought control of a 40 percent stake in Audiovisual Sport to gain access to its soccer broadcast rights. Market analysts see the rights as critical to digital television success in Spain.

Audiovisual Sport sold the exclusive rights to Canal Plus -backed CanalSatelite late last year. "CanalSatelite Digital is disposed to talk with Via Digital...to study the possibility that the football rights would not be exclusive and could be opened to other operators," Manuel Campo Vidal, who was re-elected chairman of Audiovisual Sport at a shareholders meeting, told reporters afterward.
"Logically, when dealing with the price of exclusivity, it should be studied only with Via Digital."

Soccer broadcast rights have been at the centre of a bitter battle for control of Spain's underdeveloped pay-TV market, pitting the government, one major media group and Via Digital against the leading opposition party, another big media group and CanalSatelite.

Earlier on Monday, Telefonica effectively assumed control of Antena 3 Television and its related stake in Audiovisual Sport in defiance of the European Commission. The Commission, which is studying two complaints filed by CanalSatelite against Telefonica, warned the Spanish telecoms operator last week to get EU approval before going ahead with its purchase of Antena 3.

Shareholders of the private TV station appointed Telefonica secretary general Jose Mas Millet as chairman and named three other Telefonica representatives to the board of directors. The Commission had no immediate reaction to Telefonica's move.

Audiovisual Sport is owned 40 percent by GMAF, which Telefonica now controls, and 40 percent by Sogecable, a joint venture led by France's Canal Plus and Spain's Prisa media group. Catalan television station TV3 owns 20 percent.
